newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina creates 518,000 jobs since May '96.
newsitem.headline: Argentina creates 518,000 jobs since May '96.

text.p: The Argentine economy created a total of 518,000 jobs in the year from May 1996, and 320,000 jobs since October, the Economy Ministry said Friday.
"This is the largest growth in employment since 1980, the year in which the figure began to be measured," the ministry's chief advisor Carlos Rodriguez told reporters.
But Rodriguez said that despite the strong growth in employment, the number of those looking for work only declined slightly to two million.
The government announced earlier Friday that unemployment fell to 16.1 percent in May from 17.3 percent in October.

Rodriguez said that job creation had been propelled by four factors: economic growth; a reduction in payroll taxes; increased labor market flexibility due to the use of temporary employment contracts, and state employment programs.
But he warned that moves to restrict temporary contracts being proposed by unions could slow job growth.
Rodriguez added that he expected industrial production to have grown by more than 10 percent in June compared to the same month last year.
